subject: geography
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is the main job of decomposers in nutrient cycling?
options: They produce energy from the Sun
They break down dead organisms and release nutrients into the soil
They hunt and eat primary consumers
They prevent nutrients from entering the soil
questions.explain: Decomposers such as bacteria and fungi break down dead matter, returning nutrients to the soil for plants to reuse.

questions.q: In an ecosystem, which of these is an abiotic component?
questions.explain: Abiotic means the non-living physical parts of an ecosystem, such as temperature, water, light and soil.

questions.q: Which adaptation helps a cactus survive in a hot desert?
options: Broad, flat leaves to catch rain
A thick, waxy stem to store water
questions.explain: A cactus stores water in its thick, waxy stem and has spines instead of leaves to reduce water loss.

questions.q: Which of the following is a leading cause of deforestation in the Amazon rainforest?
questions.explain: Cattle ranching, along with logging, mining and farming, is a major direct cause of Amazon deforestation.

questions.q: Which statement best describes the climate of a tropical rainforest?
options: Hot and dry all year round
Cold and dry all year round
Hot and wet all year round
Hot in summer and cold in winter
questions.explain: Tropical rainforests near the Equator are hot and wet throughout the year, with no distinct dry season.

questions.q: Why do many tall rainforest trees have buttress roots?
options: To support their height in thin, shallow soils
To reach sunlight at the forest floor
questions.explain: Buttress roots are large above-ground roots that give tall trees extra stability in the rainforest's thin, nutrient-poor soils.

questions.q: An animal that eats only plants is best described as a:
questions.explain: A herbivore is a primary consumer that feeds only on plants (producers).

questions.q: What is the role of producers in a food chain?
options: They convert sunlight into energy by photosynthesis
They recycle nutrients into the soil
questions.explain: Producers such as green plants make their own food from sunlight through photosynthesis, forming the base of the food chain.

questions.q: Which human activity is a major threat to global biodiversity?
questions.explain: Destroying habitats removes the homes of plants and animals, reducing the variety of life (biodiversity).

questions.q: In a tropical rainforest, the dense, continuous layer of treetops that blocks most light from reaching the ground is called the:
questions.explain: The canopy is a thick layer of treetops about 30–45m up that absorbs most of the sunlight and rainfall.

questions.q: Why is the soil in a tropical rainforest often surprisingly infertile?
options: It is too cold for plants to grow
Heavy rain leaches nutrients and most nutrients are stored in the vegetation
questions.explain: Most nutrients are held in the biomass; heavy rainfall quickly leaches the thin soil, so it is rapidly exhausted once trees are cleared.

questions.q: Why are tropical rainforests so important for the global environment?
options: They reflect sunlight back into space
They store carbon and produce oxygen
They cool the planet by producing ice
questions.explain: Rainforests act as a carbon store and 'carbon sink', and their photosynthesis releases oxygen, helping regulate the climate.
